findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() can now return null, shifting the NPE to callers
findings.body: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the group has been removed concurrently (`modelSupplier.get()` returns null). `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` previously never returned null for a live adapter, and callers treat it as a value: e.g. `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` passes it straight into `GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(...)` (producing a `subGroupCount: null` in the admin REST payload) and any caller that compares/unboxes the result (`count > 0`, `long c = group.getSubGroupsCount()`) will throw NPE at a point further from the cause. Returning `0L` (or re-checking invalidation and delegating) would keep the contract intact; if null is intentional, the `GroupModel` javadoc should document it and the known consumers should be audited.

findings.title: Same concurrent-removal NPE remains in the three getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: Lines 256, 262 and 268 (`getSubGroupsStream(search, first, max)`, `getSubGroupsStream(first, max)`, `getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, first, max)`) call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check. `modelSupplier` resolves via `cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(realm, cached.getId())`, which returns null exactly in the race this PR fixes for `getSubGroupsCount()` (group deleted while a cached adapter is still in use). So listing subgroups concurrently with a group deletion still throws NPE inside the cache layer, i.e. the fix is incomplete for the reported issue.

findings.title: populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups dereferences a possibly-null parent group
findings.body: `session.groups().getGroupById(realm, currGroup.getParentId())` can return null when the parent group is removed while the hierarchy is being built (the very concurrency scenario this PR targets). `parentModel` is then passed to `groupEvaluator.canView(parentModel)` (line 51), `toRepresentation(groupEvaluator, parentModel, full)` (line 57) and `populateSubGroupCount(parentModel, parent)` (line 60), all of which dereference it, producing an NPE/500 from the admin groups endpoint. A null check that breaks out of the while loop (and drops the orphaned child) is needed.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion races with the thread it validates
findings.body: `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` starts a reader thread and asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty immediately after `deletedAll.set(true)`. The reader can still be in the middle of an HTTP request at that moment, so an exception recorded after the assertion is silently lost (false pass), and a failure recorded in a later test's execution window produces confusing noise. The thread is also left running after the test method returns, continuing to call `managedRealm.admin()` while the test framework may already be tearing down/closing the admin client. The thread should be joined (with a timeout) before asserting, and the test should fail with the captured exception's stack trace.

findings.title: Shared admin client used from two threads and no guarantee the race is hit
findings.body: The reader thread and the main thread both use `managedRealm.admin()` (the same injected Keycloak admin client / underlying JAX-RS client), which is not documented as thread-safe for concurrent request submission; failures from client-side state corruption would be indistinguishable from the server-side NPE this test is meant to catch. In addition the test has no synchronization that guarantees a read overlaps a delete, so it can pass even with the bug present (and the created groups are not registered with `managedRealm.cleanup()`, so a mid-test failure leaves 100 groups behind for other tests in the realm).
